from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph", [
            "A planar graph has no crossing edges.",
            "Components: Vertices, Edges, and Faces.",
            "Example: Spider-web graph structure."
        ])

        # Define graph components
        v_coords = [self.grid['B3'], self.grid['B5'], self.grid['D2'], self.grid['D6'], self.grid['F3'], self.grid['F5']]
        vertices = VGroup(*[Dot(coord, color=WHITE) for coord in v_coords])
        edges = VGroup(
            Line(v_coords[0], v_coords[1], color=WHITE),
            Line(v_coords[1], v_coords[3], color=WHITE),
            Line(v_coords[3], v_coords[5], color=WHITE),
            Line(v_coords[5], v_coords[4], color=WHITE),
            Line(v_coords[4], v_coords[2], color=WHITE),
            Line(v_coords[2], v_coords[0], color=WHITE),
            Line(v_coords[0], v_coords[3], color=WHITE),
            Line(v_coords[2], v_coords[5], color=WHITE)
        )
        graph = VGroup(edges, vertices)
        graph_label = Text("G", font_size=24, color=WHITE).next_to(graph, UP)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW), Create(graph), Write(graph_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        v_label = Text("V", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(vertices, LEFT)
        e_label = Text("E", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(edges, RIGHT)
        
        self.play(vertices.animate.set_color(RED), Write(v_label))
        self.play(edges.animate.set_color(GREEN), Write(e_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Highlight a face
        face = Polygon(v_coords[0], v_coords[1], v_coords[3], v_coords[2], color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        f_label = Text("F", font_size=20, color=BLUE).move_to(face.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(face), Write(f_label))
        
        # Draw closed curve
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=PURPLE).move_to(graph.get_center())
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Euler’s Characteristic Formula", [
            "Euler's formula: V - E + F = 2.",
            "Connected planar graphs follow this rule.",
            "Face F includes the infinite outer region.",
            "Example: Triangle has 3V, 3E, 2F.",
            "Calculation confirms 3 - 3 + 2 = 2."
        ])
        
        # Setup triangle
        v1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v2 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v3 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        e12 = Line(v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e23 = Line(v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        e31 = Line(v3.get_center(), v1.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        triangle = VGroup(e12, e23, e31, v1, v2, v3)
        self.place_in_area(triangle, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        formula = MathTex("V", "-", "E", "+", "F", "=", "2")
        formula.set_color_by_tex("V", RED)
        formula.set_color_by_tex("E", GREEN)
        formula.set_color_by_tex("F", BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'A3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(triangle))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Flash(formula[4], color=BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Flash(formula[0], color=RED), Flash(formula[2], color=GREEN), Flash(formula[4], color=BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        circle = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Concept of Dual Graphs", [
            "Dual graph transformation: Place vertices in faces.", 
            "Connect vertices if faces share an edge.", 
            "Analogy: Sensors in rooms connect through doors."
        ])
        
        # Original graph setup
        nodes = {
            "v1": [0, 1], "v2": [1, 1], "v3": [0, 0], "v4": [1, 0]
        }
        edges = [("v1", "v2"), ("v2", "v4"), ("v4", "v3"), ("v3", "v1"), ("v1", "v4")]
        
        graph_vgroup = VGroup()
        node_mobs = {k: Dot(color=WHITE) for k in nodes}
        for k, pos in nodes.items():
            node_mobs[k].move_to(self.grid["C3"] + np.array([pos[0]-0.5, pos[1]-0.5, 0]))
            graph_vgroup.add(node_mobs[k])
            
        edge_mobs = VGroup()
        for u, v in edges:
            edge_mobs.add(Line(node_mobs[u].get_center(), node_mobs[v].get_center(), color=WHITE))
        graph_vgroup.add(edge_mobs)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(graph_vgroup))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFA500"))
        
        # Place vertices in faces (2 faces)
        dual_nodes = [Dot(color="#FFA500").move_to(self.grid["B3"]), Dot(color="#FFA500").move_to(self.grid["D3"])]
        dual_vgroup = VGroup(*dual_nodes)
        self.play(FadeIn(dual_vgroup))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        dual_edge = Line(dual_nodes[0].get_center(), dual_nodes[1].get_center(), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(dual_edge))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Duality Connection", [
            "Original G's faces become Dual G*'s vertices.",
            "Original G's vertices become Dual G*'s faces.",
            "Duality preserves Euler's structural relationship.",
            "Square: 4V, 4E, 2F morphs correctly.",
            "Duality maintains V - E + F = 2."
        ])
        
        # Create Graph G (Square)
        vertices_g = [UP+LEFT, UP+RIGHT, DOWN+RIGHT, DOWN+LEFT]
        edges_g = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 0)]
        g = Graph(list(range(4)), edges_g, layout={i: v for i, v in enumerate(vertices_g)}, vertex_config={"radius": 0.1, "color": WHITE}, edge_config={"stroke_width": 4, "color": WHITE})
        
        # Create Dual G*
        g_dual = Graph([0, 1], [(0, 1)], layout={0: ORIGIN, 1: UP*2+RIGHT*2}, vertex_config={"radius": 0.1, "color": "#FFA500"}, edge_config={"stroke_width": 4, "color": "#FFA500"})
        
        objs = VGroup(g, g_dual)
        self.place_in_area(objs, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(g), FadeIn(g_dual))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFA500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFA500")
        self.play(Indicate(g))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FFFF")
        label = Text("V=4, E=4, F=2", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A1")
        self.play(Write(label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(FadeOut(label))
        eq = MathTex("V - E + F = 2", color="#00FFFF").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(eq, "A1")
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", [
            "Euler's formula defines planar graph DNA.",
            "Duality acts as a powerful mirror tool.",
            "3D model unfolds into 2D planar graph."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        euler = MathTex("V - E + F = 2", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(euler, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)

            Circle(radius=0.3, color=RED),

outline.topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Characteristic and Duality

sections.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
sections.content: Define a planar graph as a graph that can be drawn in a plane without any edges crossing. Introduce key components: Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F).
sections.example: Visualize a 'Spider-web' diagram: The center is a vertex, the threads are edges, and the gaps between threads are the faces.

sections.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
sections.content: Introduce the fundamental theorem: V - E + F = 2. Explain that this formula holds for all connected planar graphs, where F includes the infinite outer region.
sections.example: Animate a triangle: 3 vertices, 3 edges, 2 faces (inside + outside). Calculation: 3 - 3 + 2 = 2. It holds!

sections.title: Concept of Dual Graphs
sections.content: Explain the transformation process: Place a vertex in every face of the original graph and connect two new vertices if their corresponding faces share an edge.
sections.example: A 'Robot Mapping' analogy: If rooms in a house are the faces, placing a sensor (vertex) in each room and connecting sensors through doors (edges) creates the Dual Graph.

sections.title: The Duality Connection
sections.content: Demonstrate how the properties of the original graph (G) relate to its dual (G*): The number of faces of G becomes the number of vertices of G*, and vice-versa.
sections.example: Show a square graph (V=4, E=4, F=2) morphing into its dual: The 2 faces become 2 vertices, and the 4 vertices become 4 faces. The V - E + F = 2 relationship remains preserved.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Synthesize that Euler's formula is the 'DNA' of planar graphs and duality is the 'mirror image' tool used in network flow and map coloring.
sections.example: Final slide: A 3D cube model unfolding into a 2D planar graph, instantly calculating V, E, and F to verify its structural integrity.
